 Norfolk travel agency Wroxham Travel ceases trading
 Business 
 Norfolk 
 By 
 Hallie Taylor
 Live Reporter 
 Share
 0 Comments 
 Wroxham Travel has ceased trading after nearly four decades in business. File photo of holidaymakers at Stansted Airport (Image: PA Wire/Yui Mok) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 A Norfolk-based travel agency has ceased trading after nearly 40 years in business.
 Wroxham Travel, based in Norwich with branches in Hoveton and Aylsham, officially closed on October 30.
 The company offered a wide range of holidays, including UK breaks, short-haul and long-haul trips, and ocean and river cruises.
 The Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA) has confirmed that the closure is being treated as a financial failure.
 An ABTA spokesman said: "We are sorry to inform you that Wroxham Travel has ceased trading with effect from October 30.
 "We are now treating this as a financial failure.
 "If you booked a holiday through Wroxham Travel, the tour operator or principal business with whom Wroxham Travel booked your holiday will be named on your paperwork (or ATOL certificate if it was a flight-inclusive holiday; this would be stated on your ATOL certificate under 'who is protecting your trip').
 "To ensure your holiday can continue as planned, you will need to contact the credit control department of your tour operator or other principal travel business with whom you have a contract.
 "Your booking should continue as normal and they will be your direct point of contact."
